Q: How to get the size of an array in lua A:

To get the size of an arraytbl, use #tbl.

You forgot to wrap items into {}. For now you assigned results to table with Address 1, table with Address 2 is ignored because you didn't assign it to anything (due to mistake)

Wrap it like this:

results = {
    -- items here separated by comma
}

Quick note: table.getn is deprecated and identical to #tbl, you can also use for k,v in ipairs(results) do. Third parameter of for statement is optional and defaults to 1.

for i = 1, #results do
    if results[i].type_address == "RESIDENCIAL" then
    -- etc
end

-- or
for k, v in ipairs(results) do
    if v.type_address == "RESIDENCIAL" then
    -- etc
end

Q: Why can't column be found? No ggplot2? A:

Could be a syntax issue; see if this works:

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(data = dowell_raw, mapping = aes(x = factor(borh), y = bois, fill = factor(borh))) +
geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.1), color = "black") +
scale_fill_manual(values = c("coral", "skyblue"), name = "Treatment") +
labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Species Richness")

If you get the same error, you'll need to provide additional debugging details in order to find a solution, e.g. see https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example

Q: How to check if **any** element exists in an `std::vector` at a given index A:

You cannot do it if you don't do some work on your data-structure, for every element in vector is initialized.

The simplist and quickest way I think, is to store a std::vector<bool> of the same size to store whether a element is not only initialized, but "modified" later as well.

If you worry that you may forget to set the other vector, bind them together:

std::vector<std::pair<std::pair<int, int>, bool>> a;

If you still think this is too ugly, you may have to implement your own simple optional

Q: Postgres "Error: SASL: SCRAM-SERVER-FIRST-MESSAGE: client password must be a string" A:

I had the same problem, apparently the config didn't recognize the before password so I had to create a new one on the terminal

sudo -u postgres psql 

ALTER USER username WITH PASSWORD 'your new password with quotes around';

not only that, because I was using pgAdmin, for it to connect I had to close and then open so I can input the new password. After that everything just started working.
